identity.title: Simultaneous radio and optical polarimetry of GRB 191221B afterglow

paper_type_evidence.quote: we report the first coordinated simultaneous polarimetry in the optical and radio bands for the afterglow associated with the typical long GRB 191221B.

evidence.quote: The redshift was measured as $z =1.148$ based on metal absorption lines in the optical afterglow observed by VLT/X-shooter(cite: gcn26553).
The redshift was measured as $z =1.148$ based on metal absorption lines in the optical afterglow observed by VLT/X-shooter(cite: gcn26553).

question.value: Is the radio (97.5 GHz) polarization of the GRB 191221B afterglow depolarized relative to the optical, and what does this say about magnetic field configuration and cool electrons / jet energy?

evidence.quote: show that the emission is depolarized in the radio band compared to the optical one.

bands.value: Band 3, 97.5 GHz polarization; photometry at 145 and 203 GHz

evidence.quote: Four epochs (0.5, 1.5, 2.5, and 9.5 days) of observations were performed with the polarization mode at 97.5 GHz (i.e., Band 3).
A total of 11 epochs of radio observations were conducted using the Atacama Large Millimetre/submillimetre Array (ALMA) and Atacama Compact Array

observing_dates.value: 11 epochs from 0.5 to ~33 days after burst

evidence.quote: Polarimetric observations were acquired using the Focal Reducer and low dispersion Spectrograph (FORS2) mounted on the VLT.

provided.value: Spectra at ~10 and ~34 hr to derive extinction

evidence.quote: The VLT also obtained X-shooter spectra for the afterglow of GRB 191221B at $\sim 10$ and $\sim 34$ hr after the GRB onset.
The X-ray data obtained by the *Swfit*/XRT were collected from the UK Swift Science Data Centre
The values for 0.121 and 0.417 days were derived in the wavelength range of $R$ band based on data reported by Buckley et al (2021)

what.value: Prompt emission E_iso and E_peak from Konus-Wind

evidence.quote: $E_{\gamma, {\rm iso}}$ = $(3.6 \pm 0.4)\times10^{53}$ erg

pipeline_or_manual.value: Raw data reduced at EA-ARC with CASA

evidence.quote: The raw data were reduced at the East Asian ALMA Regional Center (EA-ARC) using CASA (version 5.6.1)(cite: casa).
using CASA (version 5.6.1)(cite: casa)

flux_calibrator.value: J1037-2934 (bandpass and flux); J1036-3744 phase; J1058+0133 polarization

evidence.quote: the bandpass and flux were calibrated using observations of J1037-2934, and J1036-3744 was used for the phase calibration.
We further performed interactive CLEAN deconvolution imaging with self-calibration.

task.value: Interactive CLEAN of Stokes I, Q, U maps

evidence.quote: The Stokes $I$, $Q$, and $U$ maps were CLEANed with an appropriate number of CLEAN iterations after the final round of self-calibration.
More details on polarimetric data analysis are reported in Covino et al. (2003)(cite: covino03) and Wiersema et al. (2012)(cite: wiersema12).

inherited.from_reference: Covino et al. 2003 (cite: covino03); Wiersema et al. 2012 (cite: wiersema12)

unstated_but_needed: tclean parameters: weighting/robust, cell size, image size, masks
Beam sizes and image rms values
Fitting method/priors for the afterglow model and light curve broken power law
Numerical afterglow polarization code is not public

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA Stokes I, Q, U

method.value: CASA reduction, interactive CLEAN with self-calibration, derive PD and PA from Q, U, I

evidence.quote: The quantities that can be derived from the polarization maps are the polarized intensity ($\sqrt{Q^2+U^2}$), polarization degree ($100\sqrt{Q^2+U^2}/I$ %, PD)

validation.value: Phase calibrator polarization stability <0.02%, consistent with 0.033% systematic

evidence.quote: we confirm that the stability of linear polarization degree is $<$0.02 %

method.value: Fit X-shooter UVB spectrum with power law plus SMC/LMC/MW extinction; Serkowski-law fit; X-ray N_H via XSPEC

evidence.quote: We fit the afterglow spectrum in this wavelength range by a simple power-law affected by rest-frame extinction

validation.value: Compared with other GRBs with polarimetry

evidence.quote: There are 8 known-$z$ GRB afterglows, including GRB 191221B, available with optical polarimetry and *Swift* X-ray observations.

analysis_steps.goal: Model afterglow light curves and SED

method.value: Numerical forward-shock synchrotron model with Blandford-McKee solution, equal arrival time surface, fixed theta_j; adjust parameters to fit radio-optical-X-ray data

evidence.quote: We performed numerical calculations of flux from the shock with a fixed $\theta_j$ which evolves as the Blandford-McKee (BM) self-similar solution

assumptions.value: Uniform density medium, energy injection E_iso propto t^0.25

evidence.quote: the ambient density is uniform and the energy continues to be injected to the shock by long activity of the central engine

validation.value: Model also explains X-ray and optical

evidence.quote: The model also explains the X-ray and optical afterglows

method.value: Compare plasma-scale anisotropic field model and Faraday depolarization by cool electrons (one-zone, N random cells) with PD and PA data

evidence.quote: the plasma in the visible region consist of $N$ random cells in each of which magnetic field is ordered.

used_for.value: ALMA and ACA calibration and imaging

evidence.quote: The ACA data were flagged, calibrated, and imaged with standard procedures with CASA (version 5.6.1).
Using the software XSPEC 12, we perform spectral fitting
We used custom software tools based on the python astropy library
linear polarization degree (PD) of 1.3 $\pm$ 0.2 %
polarization angle (PA) of 61.6 $\pm$ 6.3 deg

results_numeric.quantity: Radio PD upper limit at 97.5 GHz

evidence.quote: The ALMA observation put the upper limit on PD of 0.6% with $3\sigma$ confidence level at 97.5 GHz.
constrained the range of PA as 37.7$-$52.3 deg with $1\sigma$ confidence level
a break-time at $3.77\pm 0.35$ days
$\alpha = 0.26\pm 0.02$ (before the break)
$\alpha = -1.62\pm 0.13$ (after the break)

results_numeric.quantity: Upper limit on non-thermal electron fraction f

evidence.quote: This leads to an upper limit $f \lesssim 0.3$.
E$_{\rm B-V} < 0.038$ (95% upper limit)

findings_qualitative.value: Radio emission is depolarized relative to optical; PAs differ; SSA does not explain it.

evidence.quote: this simultaneous polarimetry between optical and radio bands indicates depolarization in the radio band.

claims.hypothesis: Radio emission is depolarized relative to optical
claims.experiment: Simultaneous ALMA 97.5 GHz and VLT R-band polarimetry at 2.5 d

evidence.quote: The ALMA observation put the upper limit on PD of 0.6% with $3\sigma$ confidence level at 97.5 GHz.

claims.hypothesis: Plasma-scale (Weibel) anisotropic field explains the depolarization
claims.experiment: Numerical polarization model vs PD, PA and temporal evolution
claims.result: Predicts same PA or 90 deg difference and too high early PD

evidence.quote: The difference in the observed PA at the radio and optical bands (the bottom panel of Figure [1](#polspec)) does not support this model.

claims.hypothesis: Faraday depolarization by cool electrons explains it

evidence.quote: indicate the existence of cool electrons that increase the estimate of jet kinetic energy by a factor of $>$ 4

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Reverse shock origin of radio emission rejected as requiring eps_e ~0.53 or ~1

evidence.quote: requires $\epsilon_e \sim 0.53$. This value is unusually high

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Dust-induced optical polarization disfavored by low extinction

evidence.quote: an intrinsic origin (i.e., due to the afterglow) of the observed polarisation compared to the dust-induced hypothesis appears to be more in agreement with the data.

limitations_admitted.value: PA difference between radio and optical only ~90% significant

evidence.quote: the PA between radio and optical is different at $\sim$90% confidence level.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only one epoch of simultaneous polarimetry; radio PD only an upper limit
Model parameters are degenerate and uncertainties not given
Faraday model one-zone and PA difference only qualitatively explained

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA data in ALMA Science Archive; VLT in ESO archive

evidence.quote: The ALMA data are available at ALMA Science Archive. The VLT data are available at ESO Science Archive Facility.
The theoretical calculation code of flux and polarization used in this work is not publicly available.
